examples.question_text: A car travels $14\,000\text{ km}$ annually and uses $7.0\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$. Fuel costs $\$1.80$ per litre. Calculate its annual fuel cost.

A car travels $12\,000\text{ km}$ annually, using $6.5\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$ with fuel at $\$2.00$ per litre. Annual registration and CTP cost $\$840$, insurance costs $\$760$, two services cost $\$260$ each, and tyres cost $\$280$. Calculate its total annual running cost.

A vehicle's annual running cost is $\$5720$, including $\$1320$ of depreciation. It travels $22\,000\text{ km}$ annually. Calculate (a) its cost per kilometre including depreciation, (b) its cost per kilometre excluding depreciation, and (c) its average weekly cost including depreciation. Use $52$ weeks per year.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}\text{Cost per kilometre} &=\frac{\$5720}{22\,000}\\&=\$0.26\text{/km}\end{align*}$

(b)
$\begin{align*}\text{Cost excluding depreciation} &=\$5720-\$1320\\&=\$4400\\\text{Cost per kilometre} &=\frac{\$4400}{22\,000}\\&=\$0.20\text{/km}\end{align*}$

(c)
$\begin{align*}\text{Weekly cost} &=\frac{\$5720}{52}\\&=\$110.00\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Two cars each travel $16\,000\text{ km}$ annually. Car A uses $8.0\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$ with fuel at $\$1.90\text{/L}$ and annual servicing of $\$560$. Car B uses $6.0\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$ with fuel at $\$2.00\text{/L}$ and annual servicing of $\$800$. Their registration and insurance costs are identical. Which car costs less for fuel and servicing, and by how much annually?
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Fuel cost A} &=\frac{16\,000}{100}\times8.0\times\$1.90\\&=\$2432\\\text{Total A} &=\$2432+\$560\\&=\$2992\\\text{Fuel cost B} &=\frac{16\,000}{100}\times6.0\times\$2.00\\&=\$1920\\\text{Total B} &=\$1920+\$800\\&=\$2720\\\text{Difference} &=\$2992-\$2720\\&=\$272\end{align*}$

Car B costs $\$272$ less annually. Equal registration and insurance costs do not change the difference.

examples.question_text: A van travels $45\,000\text{ km}$ during a year that starts immediately after a major service. A minor service is due every $7500\text{ km}$ and costs $\$180$. A major service is due every $15\,000\text{ km}$ and costs $\$480$, replacing the minor service at that interval. Include the service due at the year's ending kilometre reading. Annual fuel costs $\$5400$, registration and CTP cost $\$1050$, and insurance costs $\$1250$. Calculate the total annual operating cost.
examples.solution_text:
Minor services occur at $7500$, $22\,500$ and $37\,500\text{ km}$ after the start. Major services occur at $15\,000$, $30\,000$ and $45\,000\text{ km}$ after the start.

$\begin{align*}\text{Servicing cost} &=3\times\$180+3\times\$480\\&=\$1980\\\text{Total annual cost} &=\$5400+\$1050+\$1250+\$1980\\&=\$8680\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A driver spends $\$2520$ on fuel during a year at an average price of $\$1.75$ per litre. The car uses $7.2\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$. Calculate the distance travelled.

A family budgets $\$115$ per week for vehicle running costs. Its annual expenses are fuel $\$2900$, registration and CTP $\$850$, insurance $\$750$, servicing $\$620$, and tyres $\$340$. Using $52$ weeks per year, determine whether the family stays within budget and by how much.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Annual budget} &=52\times\$115\\&=\$5980\\\text{Actual annual cost} &=\$2900+\$850+\$750+\$620+\$340\\&=\$5460\\\text{Amount under budget} &=\$5980-\$5460\\&=\$520\end{align*}$

The family stays within budget by $\$520$.

examples.question_text: Car A costs $\$24\,000$ to purchase and $\$3900$ annually to run. Car B costs $\$29\,000$ to purchase and $\$2900$ annually to run. Assume these annual costs remain constant and all other factors are equal. Find (a) when their total purchase and running costs are equal and (b) the smallest number of completed whole years after which Car B costs less.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}\text{Extra purchase cost of B} &=\$29\,000-\$24\,000\\&=\$5000\\\text{Annual running saving} &=\$3900-\$2900\\&=\$1000\\\text{Time to equal total costs} &=\frac{\$5000}{\$1000\text{/year}}\\&=5\text{ years}\end{align*}$

(b) The costs are equal after $5$ years. Car B first costs less after $6$ completed whole years.

examples.question_text: An employee drives $28\,000\text{ km}$ annually. The car uses $7.5\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$ with fuel at $\$1.80\text{/L}$. Annual registration and CTP cost $\$850$, insurance costs $\$900$, maintenance costs $\$1100$, and depreciation is $\$2800$. The employer reimburses $\$0.40$ per kilometre. Does the reimbursement cover the total annual operating cost, including depreciation? Calculate the difference.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Fuel used} &=\frac{28\,000}{100}\times7.5\\&=2100\text{ L}\\\text{Fuel cost} &=2100\times\$1.80\\&=\$3780\\\text{Total operating cost} &=\$3780+\$850+\$900+\$1100+\$2800\\&=\$9430\\\text{Reimbursement} &=28\,000\times\$0.40\\&=\$11\,200\\\text{Surplus} &=\$11\,200-\$9430\\&=\$1770\end{align*}$

The reimbursement covers the total operating cost, with a surplus of $\$1770$.

Six service intervals end within 45,000 km. Major services replace minor services at intervals 2, 4 and 6, leaving three of each. Servicing costs 3 × $180 + 3 × $480 = $1980. Total: $5400 + $1050 + $1250 + $1980 = $8680.
